title: Streaming Word Count
prompt: Implement count_words(paths) where paths is a list of text files. Stream every file line by line (never read_text the whole file) and return the total count of whitespace-separated tokens across all files.

tests.name: counts across files
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
a = d / 'a.txt'; a.write_text('one two three', encoding='utf-8')
b = d / 'b.txt'; b.write_text('four' + chr(10) + 'five six', encoding='utf-8')
assert count_words([a, b]) == 6
tests.hint: Iterate each file line by line; split and accumulate.

tests.name: empty files contribute zero
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'e.txt'; p.write_text('', encoding='utf-8')
assert count_words([p]) == 0
tests.hint: No tokens in an empty stream.

tests.name: streams instead of slurping
tests.code:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
p = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'big.txt'
p.write_text('a b c' + chr(10) + 'd e', encoding='utf-8')
def _no_slurp(self, *a, **k):
    raise AssertionError('read_text() slurps the whole file - stream line by line instead')
Path.read_text = _no_slurp
assert count_words([p]) == 5
tests.hint: read_text() loads the entire file into memory; iterate the file object line by line.
